question: In a June 2023 NewsNation interview, then US Senator Marco Rubio said that several current or former government personnel had approached the US Senate Intelligence Committee with what he called ‘firsthand knowledge or firsthand claims’ concerning matters related to unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP). He added that many had held high-level security clearances and senior government positions. The current US Government has been regularly releasing tranches of documents on this issue. 1.
Has the Commission verified the documents and the statements of its US counterparts on this issue?
Does the Commission consider the publications of the US administration to be at all serious?
Does the Commission rule out the existence of UAP/UFOs?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.8.2026) The area of unidentified anomalous phenomenon (UAP) is considered a competence of the Member States, allowing them to address these phenomena according to the national security needs. For example, France has established the Unidentified Aerospace Phenomena Research and Information Group (GEIPAN).

Therefore, the Commission is not in a position to verify any document or make any consideration regarding publications on this topic. The Commission and the High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy/Vice President remain dedicated to collaborating with stakeholders to ensure the safety and security of the space environment.
